messages:
maria: Heads up — our edge-runtime unit tests started failing in CI after the ESM/exports change. Both Jest and Vitest runs hit 'Cannot use import statement outside a module' when attempting to mock the SDK's internal auth helper.

kai: ugh. which test suite? link?

maria: /packages/edge-sdk/tests/auth-retry.test.ts
CI log excerpt:```
Error: Cannot use import statement outside a module
 at Object.compile (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:999:30)
 at Object.Module._extensions..js (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:1027:10)
 at require (internal/modules/cjs/helpers.js:72:18)
 at Object.<anonymous> (/workspace/packages/edge-sdk/__mocks__/fetch.ts:2:1)
```

james: are we running jest with transform set to ts-jest? after ESM flip the default CJS transform breaks.

lee: For Vitest we use esbuild. Vitest handles ESM better but mocks sometimes need vitest config with deps.inline or dependency optimization turned on.

sam: I reproduced locally. The failure happens when we mock a named export from a file that re-exports from an ESM-only package. The hoisting behavior differs between jest and vitest.

kai: can you paste the mock?

maria:```
// __mocks__/auth.ts
import { getToken } from '../../src/auth';
export const getToken = vi.fn(() => Promise.resolve('tok'));
```

maria: in CI the mock file is executed under CJS, so that import line trips. Locally with node 18+ and ESM enabled it works.

james: Try changing the mock to use dynamic import or require. e.g. for Jest (CJS runner) do:```
const real = require('../../src/auth');
module.exports = { getToken: jest.fn(() => Promise.resolve('tok')) };
```
but that won't fly for Vitest/ESM.

lee: Another pattern: keep the mock as ESM but tell Jest to use babel-jest or ts-jest with useESM: true. In package.json for the package set "type": "module"? That cascades though.

sam: I tried adding a per-package jest.config.cjs with transform: {'^.+\\.ts$': 'ts-jest'} and ts-jest's useESM flag, but our monorepo tsconfig paths plus babel pipeline made sourcemaps unhappy and some tests timed out.

maria: The real kicker: the edge runtime tests spawn a node process using --experimental-vm-modules and expect ESM. The test harness runs under CJS in CI (due to how we call jest in the root). So mismatch.

kai: possible fixes (ranked):
1) Move edge-suite tests to run with Vitest (native ESM) in CI job.
2) Keep Jest but set up per-package ESM runner config (ts-jest useESM + node 18).
3) Convert mocks to conditional wrappers that detect environment (module vs require). Ugly though.

james: I like 1) but migration effort could be non-trivial for some test helpers. Also GH actions caching for vitest snapshots is different.

lee: Quick workaround: add a transform for __mocks__ files to compile ESM->CJS for the runner. Example vitest config snippet I used:```
// vitest.config.ts
export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    deps: { inline: ['edge-sdk'] },
    esbuild: { target: 'es2020' },
  },
});
```

sam: For Jest I hacked a pretest step that rewrites imports in __mocks__ to use dynamic import if process.env.JEST_WORKER_ID exists. Not ideal.

maria: Anyone seen issues with typings too? After ESM flip TS complains about missing default export when mocking named exports.

kai: yes, when you use `vi.mock('pkg', () => ({ default: {} }))` types can get confused. Use `as unknown as typeof import('pkg')` in tests or update tsconfig to allowSyntheticDefaultImports.

james: We should document a recommended pattern in devex docs: a small section per runner covering 'how to mock our SDK' with examples for Jest (CJS), Jest(ESM), and Vitest. That'll reduce ad-hoc hacks.

lee: Agreed. Also add a CI job matrix that runs the edge-sdk tests under both runners for a week during rollout. Catch these early.

dev-bot: Note: created ticket INF-1029 to track 'edge-sdk test ESM/CJS mock breakages' and assigned to @maria.

ci-bot: CI: workflow run #5124 failed on job edge-tests (see https://ci.internal/runs/5124).

maria: I'll start a small doc and prototype switching the edge suite to Vitest in a feature branch. Will ping for review. Thanks for triage. :pray:

kai: happy to help with vitest config and snapshot porting.

james: ping me for ts-jest tuning if we go that route.

lee: also add notes about sourcemap noise — ts-jest + ESM currently produces line offsets in our stack traces. We should add a troubleshooting snippet. :face_with_monocle:

sam: ok I'll open a PR with a minimal vitest config and a converted test as proof-of-concept.

maria: thanks — will follow up in ticket INF-1029.
